prompt: a geography-textbook oblique diagram of a river meander. At the bend, the river current erodes the OUTER bank and deposits sediment on the INNER bank. Draw the OUTER bank of the bend as a STEEP ERODED CUT BANK -- a dark steep river cliff with hatching / shadow along the water edge -- and draw the INNER bank as a GENTLE SANDY POINT BAR -- a pale low crescent of sand (a beach). Label the two banks at the bend with a big letter A and a big letter B. Key fact: the OUTER bank of a meander is the steep eroded cut bank and the INNER bank is the gentle sandy point bar. Do NOT reverse them (the bend does NOT erode the inside). Make the steep cliff and the sandy beach clearly, unmistakably different. Clean, readable diagram.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a labelled river-meander (river-bend) diagram whose two banks at the bend are marked A and B? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
